transcript: One of the things as a farmer, I just find very, very concerning knowing that we have a lot of hungry people in this country and coming to find out that fully 40% of the food that's produced in our country is wasted. Our legislation that I'm happy to co-sponsor with Ms. Pingree from the State of Maine is an effort to bring some clarity, I guess, and the confusion on what those dates on food products actually mean. Right now, there's no standardized definition for any of these dates. So best if used by freshness by all of these different things are just dates that are put on by individual companies to try to help consumers make decisions. But many times, these dates can expire and there's absolutely nothing wrong with the food product, but it gets thrown out. And so we're trying to bring some clarity, some standardization to this so people know when they look at a product what that date actually means and whether it's safe to consume or not. And so I'm very happy to be able to work and a bipartisan way to address this issue. I'm the co-chairman of the food recovery caucus, and we'll continue to work on this so that we can try to reduce the amount of food that so many resources go into the protection, whether it's land and water, all of the inputs and labor that goes into the protection of food, and then we end up tossing so much of it out. truly egregious amount of waste and time inputs and money. We really need to stop that so we can be more efficient and help feed more people.
